subject: Compensation range synthesis & local-market localization playbook
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: benchmarks@mercurycomp.com, hr@acme-analytics.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Compensation range synthesis & local-market localization playbook

Team —

As we discussed in last week's talent sync, we need a concise playbook that converts our global leveling bands into explicit offer ranges by market cohort (US coastal, US central, EU major, LATAM, APAC hub). The goal: a repeatable, low-friction checklist for recruiters and hiring managers that covers midpoint anchoring, local premium adjustments, and guidance for exceptional hires.

Deliverables I'm asking for this week:
- A single-sheet matrix that maps Level -> Base range (low/mid/high) per market cohort.
- Short decision rules for when to make an exception (+% cap, approval path).
- Comparable-market benchmarks and source notes.

I've looped in MercuryComp (benchmarks) and Acme HR (local feedback) to provide market data. Marissa — can you draft the initial matrix and a short approval flow? Vivek — I'd like a quick note on how this interacts with our Dedicated hiring credits (any constraints). Laura — will need your sign-off on the exception caps and committee flow.

I'll collate everything into a playbook doc and attach the working spreadsheet.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
VP, Talent Strategy | Redwood Inference

Attachment: comp-range-matrix-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: MercuryComp Consulting <benchmarks@mercurycomp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, hr@acme-analytics.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compensation range synthesis & local-market localization playbook

Jonas / team —

Thanks for the brief. Attached is our regional benchmarking packet (local-market-benchmarks.pdf) and a suggested slug for the Level -> Range matrix filled with market percentiles (25/50/75). Key highlights:
- US coastal markets (SF/NY/SEA) show +18–25% midpoint to US national median for senior ICs (L4+).
- EU major cities (London/Paris/Berlin) cluster around -8 to +2% vs US national median depending on purchasing power parity adjustments.
- LATAM markets skew significantly lower on base but often have higher variable comp components; we recommend keeping capped equity multipliers to preserve unit economics.

We included source notes in the PDF. Let us know if you'd like the same matrix in CSV for import into your spreadsheet.

— Sam Ortega
MercuryComp Consulting
Attachment: local-market-benchmarks.pdf (report stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, benchmarks@mercurycomp.com, hr@acme-analytics.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compensation range synthesis & local-market localization playbook

Jonas —

I've pulled the first draft into comp-range-matrix-v2.xlsx (attached) and applied MercuryComp's midpoints. Two proposed deviations I want to flag:
1) For L5 (Senior Engineer / Senior PM) in LATAM hubs where we cannot offer competitive base, I propose we increase total target comp by +7–10% via signing equity or hiring bonus rather than raising base. This keeps salary compression manageable for local teams.
2) For EU hubs, we should index the bands to a GBP/EUR-adjusted midpoint and avoid a flat dollar adjustment — otherwise local offers look misaligned with pensions/tax.

Question for Vivek: does Dedicated hiring credits (reserved capacity budget for sales/engineering hires) require special approval if we use credits for sign-on bonuses?

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Recruiting Operations

Attachment: comp-range-matrix-v2.xlsx (updated)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 14:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compensation range synthesis & local-market localization playbook

Marissa / Jonas —

Quick answer: Dedicated hiring credits can be applied to sign-on bonuses, but anything that increases Total Target Comp above the published band + 12% would require VP-level approval (Finance + Talent). So keep exception caps at <=12% whenever possible. If you need to go higher for strategic hires, file an exception request and route to Laura for final sign-off.

Also: please add a short checklist item for recruiters to confirm local benefits equivalency (pension, employer taxes, statutory leave). That is where we see most offer confusion post-accept.

Vivek
Director, Workforce Planning

Thanks for the solid draft — this is exactly the type of operational guidance we need. A few decisions and next steps: 

1) Exception cap: set firm default at +12% Total Target Comp (base + cash + sign-on). Anything above requires a written exception routed to People Ops and me.
2) LATAM approach: approve Marissa's recommendation to use signing equity/bonus up to the 10% band for L5 hires; document the preferred language in offers and the accounting treatment.
3) EU indexing: approve GBP/EUR-indexing for bands and require recruiters to run the net-pay calculator (link in the playbook) before finalizing.

Marissa — please incorporate these bullets into the playbook and push a ‘v1 published’ tag. Send me the final Drive link and I'll sign off formally. Vivek — we need the checklist item for local benefits equivalency added before we publish.

Once published, Talent Ops should update the hiring packet and the Offer Template to show the localized band values. Notify Finance and Talent Systems to consume the new matrix.

Laura Bennett
Chief People Officer | Redwood Inference
